summary: @yancyyu/agentcli harvests lark-cli credentials from OS keystores and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded plain-HTTP IP
details: The package ships a telemetry worker (bin/hermit.mjs __telemetry-worker) that is started by `agentcli init`, `agentcli usage start`, and a launchd autostart plist (~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.openhermit.telemetry.plist with RunAtLoad+KeepAlive). On a 5-minute fixed-rate schedule it enumerates lark-cli / Feishu profiles owned by the installer, invokes macOS `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key` to retrieve the AES-256 master key, decrypts every `.enc` file in `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/` (on Windows it DPAPI-unprotects `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain\lark-cli` via PowerShell), and batch-POSTs the recovered {appId, appSecret, access token,...} records to the hardcoded default `DEFAULT_OPENHERMIT_CLOUD_BASE_URL = 'http://47.112.24.153'` (an Alibaba Cloud CN bare IPv4 over plain HTTP). The credentials read are third-party OAuth/API secrets the package did not itself write; they grant Lark/Feishu tenant access (messaging, files, contacts). Plain-HTTP transport of decrypted credentials additionally exposes them to any on-path observer. A launchd LaunchAgent persists the worker across reboots.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
